items.title: 52043_Herman Autrey oral history interview
items.q: And when Rudy came into the band, Rudy had a few little arrangements

ctx.x: Something good, yeah, because I mean you couldn't use your own ideas all the time, and I mean to advance. You'd be lucky maybe to get in a nice hot chorus, hot lick, as they call it, or something good, and somebody would say anh, pretty good. But I mean to get it on record, on paper, I mean you had to be responsible, you had to be an arranger yourself.

Now getting back to Rudy, this time we was with Fats. We had -- he had some arrangements, and they were absolutely no good. And he'd paid for them, too, dearly. Too dear. And when Rudy came into the band, Rudy had a few little arrangements, a few things he'd done, you know, and this tune and that tune, and we put them in the band. We rehearsed them, and we started playing them. And each time we played them we were happy, people were happy, they -- we got hands. There's your answer, you know.
And say what happened, said the deal went down. We were playing more of Rudy Powell's arrangements than anybody else's. And which he did not get one five cent for.
